text: Linux Syslog collection goes smoothly: the Azure Monitor Agent forwards auth, authpriv, daemon, and cron facilities into the Syslog table. The firewall's CEF forwarding takes most of the day, since the firewall's export config, the relay's listener, and the AMA's collection rule all have to agree.

Mid-setup, Meridian Controls, Hartwell's firewall vendor, offers to remote in and resolve a configuration question directly. With Sentinel's go-live the same week as Renee's compliance review, Mara and Network Administrator Derek Shaw take the offer.

Derek needs a rule allowing Meridian's real range, 203.0.113.16/28, in to the admin jump host on RDP. Working against the clock, he copies an old field-office template rule and updates the source address -- but the template's /16 mask comes along unchanged.
203.0.113.16/28 covers 16 addresses. 203.0.0.0/16, what actually got saved, covers 65,536. The difference is one character in a rule with a dozen fields that all look correct.

Meridian connects, the session works perfectly, because their real IP falls inside the broad range too. Nothing about today's successful vendor call reveals that 65,520 other addresses can now reach the same RDP port.
